title: BDEW API URI Normalization and Content-Signing Conformance Test Corpus
profile: Absolute HTTP/HTTPS URIs. URI normalization follows RFC 3986 sections 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.2.2.3 and 6.2.3. Payload canonicalization follows RFC 8785. Signature-preimage integration assertions follow the supplied BDEW API specification, section 3.3, version 1.2 dated 2025-07-18.

scope.primary_target: A URI normalizer used to prepare the URI component for the BDEW signature hash.
also_included: RFC 8785 JSON payload canonicalization tests because the payload is also hashed by the signature procedure.
Signature-preimage integration assertions for component ordering, optional initialTransactionId, and required header encoding.
out_of_scope: Cryptographic key generation, certificate-chain validation, ECDSA implementation correctness, and full PKI policy validation.
HTTP request routing behavior and proxy/server path interpretation.
A complete implementation of RFC 3986 reference resolution; the URI profile here accepts absolute HTTP/HTTPS URIs only.

normalization_contract.input_profile: A syntactically valid absolute HTTP or HTTPS URI, represented as an RFC 3986 URI (ASCII syntax; non-ASCII data must be percent-encoded).
normalization_contract.output_profile: A normalized absolute HTTP or HTTPS URI string used as the input to Hash(URI).
processing_order: Parse the complete URI into scheme, authority, path, query, and fragment components before modifying any component.
Normalize percent-encoding triplets: decode only ASCII unreserved octets; uppercase hex digits in all remaining triplets.
Lowercase the scheme and host; preserve case in userinfo, path, query, and fragment.
Apply HTTP/HTTPS scheme-based normalization: remove an empty/default port; convert an empty path to '/'.
Apply RFC 3986 remove_dot_segments to the path only.
Reassemble the URI while preserving significant delimiters, empty query/fragment components, query ordering, duplicates, and all non-normalized component data.
important_non_operations: Do not convert '+' to a space.
Do not decode percent-encoded reserved characters such as %2F, %3F, %26, or %3D.
Do not lowercase path, query, fragment, or userinfo data.
Do not apply dot-segment removal to query or fragment data.
Do not silently remove an empty query or fragment delimiter.
Do not rewrite IPv6 literals using compression or another textual representation beyond lowercase hex digits.
Do not perform Unicode normalization or implicit IRI-to-URI conversion.

profile_policy_decisions.decision: Preserve and RFC 3986-normalize a fragment if one is supplied to this normalizer; do not silently strip it. The HTTP/API layer should separately ensure that a fragment is not being treated as part of an HTTP request target, because fragments are not transmitted in an HTTP request.
Reject in this strict URI profile. If callers start with IRIs, convert them to a URI using a separately specified and tested IRI-to-URI/IDNA process before calling this normalizer.

Require the port component to contain only decimal digits or be empty. Remove only the explicitly empty port and the exact scheme default (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS). This corpus does not infer equivalence for zero-padded port strings.
Accept syntactically valid userinfo and preserve its semantics; do not lowercase or remove it. The application may impose a stricter policy separately.

assumptions: The test target is a normalizer for absolute HTTP/HTTPS URIs, not a general URI-reference resolver.
The URI normalizer is used to derive the URI bytes to hash. The supplied BDEW excerpt does not explicitly require the actual HTTP request target to be rewritten to the normalized spelling.
RFC 3986 percent-encoding normalization is applied before dot-segment removal so that percent-encoded unreserved dots become complete dot segments where applicable.
Percent-encoded non-ASCII octets remain percent-encoded; this normalizer does not decode arbitrary bytes as UTF-8.
An empty query delimiter '?' and an empty fragment delimiter '#' are preserved because delimiter removal is not authorized by HTTP scheme-based normalization.
The URI test cases are normative assertions for the profile above; profile-specific policies are identified explicitly and should be reviewed against the API deployment contract.
recommended_order: Run invalid URI rejection tests first.
Verify normalization idempotence for every successful test output.

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.2.2: decode percent-encoded octets only when they represent ASCII unreserved characters ALPHA / DIGIT / '-' / '.' / '_' / '~'. Preserve percent-encoded reserved and other octets, with uppercase hexadecimal digits. Do not decode recursively.

sections.description: RFC 3986 6.2.2.3 and 5.2.4: remove complete '.' and '..' path segments using the remove_dot_segments algorithm. The query and fragment must be separated before processing the path. Percent-encoded unreserved dots are decoded before dot-segment removal; encoded slashes remain encoded and do not create path separators.

sections.description: RFC 3986 treats generic components as case-sensitive except where specifically stated. Do not reorder or reinterpret query parameters, collapse repeated slashes, decode reserved escapes, remove empty query/fragment delimiters, or perform HTML form decoding. The fragment is not subject to HTTP scheme-based normalization; this corpus preserves it rather than silently discarding it.

sections.description: Preserve authority subcomponents except for normalization explicitly allowed by RFC 3986. Lowercase the host, retain userinfo case and delimiters, lowercase IPv6 hex digits, and do not invent alternate IPv6 compression or address formatting.

equivalence_groups.meaning: Scheme and host case are normalized.
HTTP empty path, empty port, and default port normalize to the canonical root URI.
HTTPS empty path and default port normalize to the canonical root URI.

non_equivalence_pairs.reason: Query parameter order is preserved; query sorting is not authorized.
Duplicate query parameter order is preserved.
A present-empty query delimiter is significant.
A present-empty fragment delimiter is significant under RFC 3986.
Encoded reserved slash is not decoded into a path separator.

normalization_property_tests.assertion: normalize(normalize(uri)) == normalize(uri) for every valid URI test vector.
Every URI in each equivalence group normalizes to that group's expected_normalized value.
The normalized outputs for both sides of every non_equivalence_pair remain different.
Changing path/query/fragment case does not trigger lowercasing of those components.
Dot-segment text in query or fragment never changes the normalized path.
Percent-encoding normalization is not recursive; a decoded percent sign is not decoded again.
Normalization preserves query parameter order, duplicate parameters, empty fields, and separators.

implementation_notes: Use a URI parser that exposes the presence/absence of query and fragment delimiters; a parser that collapses empty components cannot pass KEEP-009/011 and NEQ-004/005.
Do not use form-urlencoded query parsing for URI normalization.
Perform normalization on parsed URI components rather than broad string substitutions.

For cryptographic reproducibility, define the exact character-to-octet encoding used for URI and HTTP header component strings in the protocol implementation. The supplied excerpt specifies the component hashes but does not, by itself, define every string-to-byte conversion detail.
For digest test vectors, compare bytes at each stage: canonical URI bytes, canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes, each component hash, concatenated M, Hash(M), and Base64 header representation.
This corpus is a broad conformance suite, not an exhaustive enumeration of every possible URI. Add fuzz/property-based tests around percent escapes, authority parsing, and dot-segment edge cases.
